image_description: A tall, wooden bookcase filled with books and various decorative objects. The bookcase has multiple shelves (approximately 6 visible levels) and appears to be made of light-to-medium stained wood. It is positioned against a plain wall, with a small plant or decorative object visible on a surface to the right.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is clearly a tall, vertical rectangular structure, significantly taller than it is wide, fitting the standard bookcase silhouette.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tall rectangular frame with horizontal divisions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertical side panels and multiple horizontal shelves create a clear rectangular frame with distinct horizontal divisions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with open front displaying books and objects.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The structure itself is symmetric in construction (left and right sides mirror each other). The front is open, revealing contents.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Multiple horizontal shelves spaced evenly from top to bottom.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are at least 5-6 distinct horizontal shelves visible, spaced relatively evenly throughout the height of the unit.

Adjustability is an internal mechanical feature (pins/holes) that cannot be definitively verified from this external view without seeing specific shelf-pin holes clearly, which are obscured by books/shadows.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood particleboard or metal with finished surface stained painted or laminated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture and color indicate a wood or wood-laminate construction with a stained finish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Front open displaying books and objects on each shelf.

The surfaces appear finished (smooth/stained). While explicit 'hardware' like knobs is absent (as there are no doors), the joinery and finish qualify as finished surfaces.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the book spines is largely illegible or nonsensical. While some shapes resemble letters, many are melted, fused, or lack coherent orthography, typical of AI generation struggling with fine text details.

artifact_observations.location: Bottom right corner of the bookcase base
artifact_observations.reasoning: The vertical support on the bottom right seems to blend slightly into the shadow/floor area, lacking a crisp edge definition compared to the left side. It's subtle but suggests slight geometric instability.

artifact_observations.location: Books on the second shelf from top
artifact_observations.reasoning: Some book spines appear to fuse together or have inconsistent thicknesses that don't align perfectly with the shelf plane, creating a slight 'melting' effect between adjacent objects.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a bookcase and not a similar shelving unit or cabinet.
To verify the structural integrity of the shelves and side panels, ensuring they are physically grounded and not floating or warped.
To check for boundary bleeding between individual books and the shelves, identifying any fusion artifacts.
To rigorously evaluate the legibility and coherence of the text on the book spines, which is a common failure point in AI images.

focus_areas: Legibility and coherence of text on book spines
Structural straightness of vertical side panels and horizontal shelves
Boundary separation between individual books and objects
Consistency of lighting and shadows within the shelf compartments
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on the book spines. Even if the classifier confirms 'bookcase', severe text gibberish is a significant artifact. Also, inspect the bottom corners of the bookcase for any warping or blending with the background, as AI often struggles with the base of tall furniture.
